review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

2:1.sourceText: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐκείναις ἐξῆλθεν δόγμα παρὰ Καίσαρος Αὐγούστου ἀπογράφεσθαι πᾶσαν τὴν οἰκουμένην.
2:1.targetText: Now in those days a decree went out from Caesar Augustus that a census should be taken of the whole empire.

targetPhrases.text: that a census should be taken of

groups.note: The infinitive ἀπογράφεσθαι ("to be registered") is rendered that a census should be taken of.
οἰκουμένην ("inhabited world") is rendered empire.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the narrative frame ἐγένετο ("it came about") untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

2:2.sourceText: αὕτη ἀπογραφὴ πρώτη ἐγένετο ἡγεμονεύοντος τῆς Συρίας Κυρηνίου.
2:2.targetText: This was the first census to take place while Quirinius was governor of Syria.

groups.note: BSB renders ἐγένετο ("took place") as was ... to take place.
The genitive absolute ἡγεμονεύοντος ("while governing") is rendered while ... was governor.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

2:3.sourceText: καὶ ἐπορεύοντο πάντες ἀπογράφεσθαι, ἕκαστος εἰς τὴν ἑαυτοῦ πόλιν.
2:3.targetText: And everyone went to his own town to register.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB expresses the distributive ἕκαστος ("each") only through the singular his own.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

2:4.sourceText: Ἀνέβη δὲ καὶ Ἰωσὴφ ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας ἐκ πόλεως Ναζαρὲθ εἰς τὴν Ἰουδαίαν εἰς πόλιν Δαυεὶδ ἥτις καλεῖται Βηθλεέμ, διὰ τὸ εἶναι αὐτὸν ἐξ οἴκου καὶ πατριᾶς Δαυείδ,
2:4.targetText: So Joseph also went up from Nazareth in Galilee to Judea, to the city of David called Bethlehem, since he was from the house and line of David.

groups.note: BSB's one from covers both ἀπό (from Galilee) and ἐκ (out of the town of Nazareth).
The relative clause ἥτις καλεῖται ("which is called") is rendered called.
διὰ τό with the infinitive means "because".

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB does not render πόλεως ("town") before Nazareth.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies in when it recasts from Galilee, out of the town of Nazareth as Nazareth in Galilee.

2:5.sourceText: ἀπογράψασθαι σὺν Μαριὰμ τῇ ἐμνηστευμένῃ αὐτῷ, οὔσῃ ἐγκύῳ.
2:5.targetText: He went there to register with Mary, who was pledged to him in marriage and was expecting a child.

groups.note: The article with the participle ἐμνηστευμένῃ ("the one betrothed") is rendered who was pledged ... in marriage.
ἐγκύῳ means "pregnant".

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB starts a new sentence by restating Joseph's journey from verse 4.
English joins the participle οὔσῃ ("being") with and.

2:6.sourceText: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ εἶναι αὐτοὺς ἐκεῖ ἐπλήσθησαν αἱ ἡμέραι τοῦ τεκεῖν αὐτήν,
2:6.targetText: While they were there, the time came for her Child to be born.

groups.note: ἐν τῷ with the infinitive means "while".
ἐπλήσθησαν ("were fulfilled") is rendered came.
ἡμέραι ("days") is rendered time.
The articular infinitive τοῦ τεκεῖν ("for her to give birth") is rendered passively, for her Child to be born.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the narrative frame ἐγένετο δέ ("and it came about") untranslated.

2:7.sourceText: καὶ ἔτεκεν τὸν υἱὸν αὐτῆς τὸν πρωτότοκον, καὶ ἐσπαργάνωσεν αὐτὸν καὶ ἀνέκλινεν αὐτὸν ἐν φάτνῃ, διότι οὐκ ἦν αὐτοῖς τόπος ἐν τῷ καταλύματι.
2:7.targetText: And she gave birth to her firstborn, a Son. She wrapped Him in swaddling cloths and laid Him in a manger, because there was no room for them in the inn.

groups.note: The verb ἐσπαργάνωσεν means "wrapped in swaddling cloths".

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB starts a new sentence with She wrapped instead of rendering καί.

2:8.sourceText: Καὶ ποιμένες ἦσαν ἐν τῇ χώρᾳ τῇ αὐτῇ ἀγραυλοῦντες καὶ φυλάσσοντες φυλακὰς τῆς νυκτὸς ἐπὶ τὴν ποίμνην αὐτῶν.
2:8.targetText: And there were shepherds residing in the fields nearby, keeping watch over their flocks by night.

groups.note: ἐν τῇ χώρᾳ τῇ αὐτῇ ("in the same region") is rendered nearby.
ἀγραυλοῦντες means "living out in the fields".

unmappedSource.reason: BSB joins the two participles with a comma instead of rendering καί.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

2:9.sourceText: καὶ ἄγγελος Κυρίου ἐπέστη αὐτοῖς καὶ δόξα Κυρίου περιέλαμψεν αὐτούς, καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν φόβον μέγαν.
2:9.targetText: Just then an angel of the Lord stood before them, and the glory of the Lord shone around them, and they were terrified.

groups.note: ἐφοβήθησαν φόβον μέγαν ("they feared a great fear") is rendered they were terrified.

2:10.sourceText: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ ἄγγελος Μὴ φοβεῖσθε· ἰδοὺ γὰρ εὐαγγελίζομαι ὑμῖν χαρὰν μεγάλην, ἥτις ἔσται παντὶ τῷ λαῷ,
2:10.targetText: But the angel said to them, “Do not be afraid! For behold, I bring you good news of great joy that will be for all the people:

groups.note: εὐαγγελίζομαι means "I announce good news".

2:11.sourceText: ὅτι ἐτέχθη ὑμῖν σήμερον Σωτήρ, ὅς ἐστιν Χριστὸς Κύριος, ἐν πόλει Δαυείδ.
2:11.targetText: Today in the city of David a Savior has been born to you. He is Christ the Lord!

groups.note: The relative ὅς ("who") is rendered He in a new sentence.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB introduces this content with the colon at the end of verse 10 instead of rendering ὅτι ("that/for").

2:12.sourceText: καὶ τοῦτο ὑμῖν σημεῖον, εὑρήσετε βρέφος ἐσπαργανωμένον καὶ κείμενον ἐν φάτνῃ.
2:12.targetText: And this will be a sign to you: You will find a baby wrapped in swaddling cloths and lying in a manger.”

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the verb; the Greek clause has none.

2:13.sourceText: καὶ ἐξαίφνης ἐγένετο σὺν τῷ ἀγγέλῳ πλῆθος στρατιᾶς οὐρανίου αἰνούντων τὸν Θεὸν καὶ λεγόντων
2:13.targetText: And suddenly there appeared with the angel a great multitude of the heavenly host, praising God and saying:

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

2:14.sourceText: Δόξα ἐν ὑψίστοις Θεῷ καὶ ἐπὶ γῆς εἰρήνη ἐν ἀνθρώποις εὐδοκίας.
2:14.targetText: “Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace to men on whom His favor rests!”

groups.note: The genitive εὐδοκίας ("of good pleasure") is rendered on whom His favor rests.

2:15.sourceText: Καὶ ἐγένετο ὡς ἀπῆλθον ἀπ’ αὐτῶν εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν οἱ ἄγγελοι, οἱ ποιμένες ἐλάλουν πρὸς ἀλλήλους Διέλθωμεν δὴ ἕως Βηθλεὲμ καὶ ἴδωμεν τὸ ῥῆμα τοῦτο τὸ γεγονὸς ὃ ὁ Κύριος ἐγνώρισεν ἡμῖν.
2:15.targetText: When the angels had left them and gone into heaven, the shepherds said to one another, “Let us go to Bethlehem and see this thing that has happened, which the Lord has made known to us.”

groups.note: BSB renders the one verb ἀπῆλθον ("went away") twice: had left them and gone into heaven.
ἀπ’ αὐτῶν ("from them") becomes the object of left.
The article with the participle γεγονός ("the thing that has happened") is rendered that has happened.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the narrative frame καὶ ἐγένετο ("and it came about") untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves the urging particle δή ("now, then") untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English splits the one Greek verb into two clauses joined by and.

2:16.sourceText: καὶ ἦλθαν σπεύσαντες, καὶ ἀνεῦραν τήν τε Μαριὰμ καὶ τὸν Ἰωσὴφ καὶ τὸ βρέφος κείμενον ἐν τῇ φάτνῃ·
2:16.targetText: So they hurried off and found Mary and Joseph and the Baby, who was lying in the manger.

groups.note: ἦλθαν σπεύσαντες ("they came, having hurried") is rendered they hurried off.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves the correlative τε ("both") untranslated.

2:17.sourceText: ἰδόντες δὲ ἐγνώρισαν περὶ τοῦ ῥήματος τοῦ λαληθέντος αὐτοῖς περὶ τοῦ παιδίου τούτου.
2:17.targetText: After they had seen the Child, they spread the message they had received about Him.

groups.note: The participle ἰδόντες ("having seen") is rendered After they had seen.
ἐγνώρισαν ("they made known") is rendered they spread.
The passive τοῦ λαληθέντος ("the thing spoken") is rendered actively, with the hearers as subject.
αὐτοῖς ("to them") becomes the subject of had received.
περὶ τοῦ παιδίου τούτου ("about this child") is rendered about Him, since BSB has already named the Child.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ untranslated.
BSB makes the message the direct object of spread instead of rendering περί ("about").

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for seen; the Greek participle has none.

2:18.sourceText: καὶ πάντες οἱ ἀκούσαντες ἐθαύμασαν περὶ τῶν λαληθέντων ὑπὸ τῶν ποιμένων πρὸς αὐτούς·
2:18.targetText: And all who heard it were amazed at what the shepherds said to them.

groups.note: The article with the participle ἀκούσαντες ("those who heard") is rendered who heard.
τῶν λαληθέντων ("the things spoken") is rendered actively as what ... said.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB turns the passive spoken by the shepherds into the active the shepherds said, so ὑπό ("by") has no counterpart.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for heard.

2:19.sourceText: ἡ δὲ Μαρία πάντα συνετήρει τὰ ῥήματα ταῦτα συνβάλλουσα ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτῆς.
2:19.targetText: But Mary treasured up all these things and pondered them in her heart.

groups.note: Same verb, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle συνβάλλουσα ("pondering") with and.
English supplies an object for pondered.

2:20.sourceText: καὶ ὑπέστρεψαν οἱ ποιμένες δοξάζοντες καὶ αἰνοῦντες τὸν Θεὸν ἐπὶ πᾶσιν οἷς ἤκουσαν καὶ εἶδον καθὼς ἐλαλήθη πρὸς αὐτούς.
2:20.targetText: The shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God for all they had heard and seen, which was just as the angel had told them.

groups.note: The passive ἐλαλήθη ("it was spoken") is rendered actively, with the angel supplied as speaker.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening καί untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves the relative οἷς ("which") unexpressed after all.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a relative frame before just as.
English supplies the speaker of the passive ἐλαλήθη.

2:21.sourceText: Καὶ ὅτε ἐπλήσθησαν ἡμέραι ὀκτὼ τοῦ περιτεμεῖν αὐτόν, καὶ ἐκλήθη τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Ἰησοῦς, τὸ κληθὲν ὑπὸ τοῦ ἀγγέλου πρὸ τοῦ συλλημφθῆναι αὐτὸν ἐν τῇ κοιλίᾳ.
2:21.targetText: When the eight days until His circumcision had passed, He was named Jesus, the name the angel had given Him before He had been conceived.

groups.note: The articular infinitive τοῦ περιτεμεῖν ("for circumcising") is rendered until ... circumcision.
ἐκλήθη τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ ("his name was called") is rendered He was named.
The neuter τὸ κληθέν ("the one called") refers back to the name and is rendered the name ... had given.
πρὸ τοῦ with the infinitive means "before".

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening καί untranslated.
BSB leaves the καί that opens the main clause after When untranslated.
BSB turns the passive called by the angel into the active the angel had given, so ὑπό ("by") has no counterpart.
BSB leaves ἐν τῇ κοιλίᾳ ("in the womb") untranslated; conceived implies it.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the one to whom the name was given.

2:22.sourceText: Καὶ ὅτε ἐπλήσθησαν αἱ ἡμέραι τοῦ καθαρισμοῦ αὐτῶν κατὰ τὸν νόμον Μωϋσέως, ἀνήγαγον αὐτὸν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα παραστῆσαι τῷ Κυρίῳ,
2:22.targetText: And when the time of purification according to the Law of Moses was complete, His parents brought Him to Jerusalem to present Him to the Lord

groups.note: ἡμέραι ("days") is rendered time.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves αὐτῶν ("their") untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject that the Greek verb ending implies.
English repeats the object of present.

2:23.sourceText: καθὼς γέγραπται ἐν νόμῳ Κυρίου ὅτι Πᾶν ἄρσεν διανοῖγον μήτραν ἅγιον τῷ Κυρίῳ κληθήσεται,
2:23.targetText: (as it is written in the Law of the Lord: “Every firstborn male shall be consecrated to the Lord”),

groups.note: διανοῖγον μήτραν ("opening the womb") is rendered firstborn.
ἅγιον ... κληθήσεται ("shall be called holy") is rendered shall be consecrated.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB marks the quotation with a colon and quotation marks instead of rendering ὅτι.

2:24.sourceText: καὶ τοῦ δοῦναι θυσίαν κατὰ τὸ εἰρημένον ἐν τῷ νόμῳ Κυρίου, ζεῦγος τρυγόνων ἢ δύο νοσσοὺς περιστερῶν.
2:24.targetText: and to offer the sacrifice specified in the Law of the Lord: “A pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons.”

groups.note: κατὰ τὸ εἰρημένον ("according to what is said") is rendered specified.
νοσσούς ("young birds") is rendered young.

2:25.sourceText: Καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄνθρωπος ἦν ἐν Ἰερουσαλὴμ ᾧ ὄνομα Συμεών, καὶ ὁ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος δίκαιος καὶ εὐλαβής, προσδεχόμενος παράκλησιν τοῦ Ἰσραήλ, καὶ Πνεῦμα ἦν Ἅγιον ἐπ’ αὐτόν·
2:25.targetText: Now there was a man in Jerusalem named Simeon, who was righteous and devout. He was waiting for the consolation of Israel, and the Holy Spirit was upon him.

groups.note: ᾧ ὄνομα ("whose name was") is rendered named.
ὁ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος ("this man") is rendered as the relative who.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves ἰδού ("behold") untranslated.
BSB turns this new clause into a relative clause instead of rendering καί.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula.

2:26.sourceText: καὶ ἦν αὐτῷ κεχρηματισμένον ὑπὸ τοῦ Πνεύματος τοῦ Ἁγίου μὴ ἰδεῖν θάνατον πρὶν ἢ ἂν ἴδῃ τὸν Χριστὸν Κυρίου.
2:26.targetText: The Holy Spirit had revealed to him that he would not see death before he had seen the Lord’s Christ.

groups.note: The passive κεχρηματισμένον ("revealed") is rendered actively, with the Holy Spirit as subject.
πρὶν ἢ ἄν is one conjunction, "before".

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening καί untranslated.
BSB turns the passive revealed by the Spirit into the active the Spirit had revealed, so ὑπό ("by") has no counterpart.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

2:27.sourceText: καὶ ἦλθεν ἐν τῷ Πνεύματι εἰς τὸ ἱερόν· καὶ ἐν τῷ εἰσαγαγεῖν τοὺς γονεῖς τὸ παιδίον Ἰησοῦν τοῦ ποιῆσαι αὐτοὺς κατὰ τὸ εἰθισμένον τοῦ νόμου περὶ αὐτοῦ,
2:27.targetText: Led by the Spirit, he went into the temple courts. And when the parents brought in the child Jesus to do for Him what was customary under the Law,

groups.note: ἐν τῷ Πνεύματι ("in the Spirit") is rendered Led by the Spirit.
ἐν τῷ with the infinitive marks time, "when".
κατὰ τὸ εἰθισμένον ("according to the custom") is rendered what was customary.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening καί untranslated.
BSB leaves αὐτούς ("they"), the subject of the infinitive, unexpressed.

2:28.sourceText: καὶ αὐτὸς ἐδέξατο αὐτὸ εἰς τὰς ἀγκάλας καὶ εὐλόγησεν τὸν Θεὸν καὶ εἶπεν
2:28.targetText: Simeon took Him in his arms and blessed God, saying:

groups.note: αὐτός ("he") is rendered by the name Simeon.
καὶ εἶπεν ("and said") is rendered saying.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening καί untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB turns the last verb into the participle saying, so καί is not rendered.

2:29.sourceText: Νῦν ἀπολύεις τὸν δοῦλόν σου, Δέσποτα, κατὰ τὸ ῥῆμά σου ἐν εἰρήνῃ·
2:29.targetText: “Sovereign Lord, as You have promised, You now dismiss Your servant in peace.

groups.note: τὸ ῥῆμά σου ("Your word") is rendered as You have promised.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

2:30.sourceText: ὅτι εἶδον οἱ ὀφθαλμοί μου τὸ σωτήριόν σου,
2:30.targetText: For my eyes have seen Your salvation,

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

2:31.sourceText: ὃ ἡτοίμασας κατὰ πρόσωπον πάντων τῶν λαῶν,
2:31.targetText: which You have prepared in the sight of all people,

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

2:32.sourceText: φῶς εἰς ἀποκάλυψιν ἐθνῶν καὶ δόξαν λαοῦ σου Ἰσραήλ.
2:32.targetText: a light for revelation to the Gentiles, and for glory to Your people Israel.”

2:33.sourceText: καὶ ἦν ὁ πατὴρ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἡ μήτηρ θαυμάζοντες ἐπὶ τοῖς λαλουμένοις περὶ αὐτοῦ.
2:33.targetText: The Child’s father and mother were amazed at what was spoken about Him.

groups.note: αὐτοῦ ("his") is rendered the Child’s.
The article with the participle λαλουμένοις ("the things being spoken") is rendered what was spoken.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening καί untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

2:34.sourceText: καὶ εὐλόγησεν αὐτοὺς Συμεὼν καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς Μαριὰμ τὴν μητέρα αὐτοῦ Ἰδοὺ οὗτος κεῖται εἰς πτῶσιν καὶ ἀνάστασιν πολλῶν ἐν τῷ Ἰσραὴλ καὶ εἰς σημεῖον ἀντιλεγόμενον
2:34.targetText: Then Simeon blessed them and said to His mother Mary:  “Behold, this Child is appointed to cause the rise and fall of many in Israel, and to be a sign that will be spoken against,

groups.note: οὗτος ("this one") is rendered this Child.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

2:35.sourceText: —καὶ σοῦ δὲ αὐτῆς τὴν ψυχὴν διελεύσεται ῥομφαία—, ὅπως ἂν ἀποκαλυφθῶσιν ἐκ πολλῶν καρδιῶν διαλογισμοί.
2:35.targetText: so that the thoughts of many hearts will be revealed— and a sword will pierce your soul as well.”

groups.note: In καὶ ... δέ, καί means "also" and δέ joins the clause.
ὅπως ἄν ("so that") is one purpose conjunction.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the intensive αὐτῆς ("yourself") untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

2:36.sourceText: Καὶ ἦν Ἄννα προφῆτις, θυγάτηρ Φανουήλ, ἐκ φυλῆς Ἀσήρ· αὕτη προβεβηκυῖα ἐν ἡμέραις πολλαῖς, ζήσασα μετὰ ἀνδρὸς ἔτη ἑπτὰ ἀπὸ τῆς παρθενίας αὐτῆς,
2:36.targetText: There was also a prophetess named Anna, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher, who was well along in years. She had been married for seven years,

groups.note: ἡμέραις πολλαῖς ("many days") is rendered years.
ζήσασα μετὰ ἀνδρός ("having lived with a husband") is rendered She had been married.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves ἀπὸ τῆς παρθενίας αὐτῆς ("from her virginity") untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies named to introduce Anna.

2:37.sourceText: καὶ αὐτὴ χήρα ἕως ἐτῶν ὀγδοήκοντα τεσσάρων, ἣ οὐκ ἀφίστατο τοῦ ἱεροῦ νηστείαις καὶ δεήσεσιν λατρεύουσα νύκτα καὶ ἡμέραν.
2:37.targetText: and then was a widow to the age of eighty-four. She never left the temple, but worshiped night and day, fasting and praying.

groups.note: ἐτῶν ("years") is rendered the age of.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB continues the sentence from verse 36 without repeating αὐτή ("she").

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a time sequence.
English supplies the copula.
English supplies a contrast with never left.

2:38.sourceText: καὶ αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ ἐπιστᾶσα ἀνθωμολογεῖτο τῷ Θεῷ καὶ ἐλάλει περὶ αὐτοῦ πᾶσιν τοῖς προσδεχομένοις λύτρωσιν Ἰερουσαλήμ.
2:38.targetText: Coming forward at that moment, she gave thanks to God and spoke about the Child to all who were waiting for the redemption of Jerusalem.

groups.note: αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ ("at that very hour") is rendered at that moment.
αὐτοῦ ("him") is rendered the Child.
The article with the participle προσδεχομένοις ("those waiting for") is rendered who were waiting for.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening καί untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

2:39.sourceText: Καὶ ὡς ἐτέλεσαν πάντα τὰ κατὰ τὸν νόμον Κυρίου, ἐπέστρεψαν εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν εἰς πόλιν ἑαυτῶν Ναζαρέθ.
2:39.targetText: When Jesus’ parents had done everything required by the Law of the Lord, they returned to Galilee, to their own town of Nazareth.

groups.note: τὰ κατά ("the things according to") is rendered required by.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening καί untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject that the Greek verb ending implies.

2:40.sourceText: Τὸ δὲ παιδίον ηὔξανεν καὶ ἐκραταιοῦτο πληρούμενον σοφίᾳ, καὶ χάρις Θεοῦ ἦν ἐπ’ αὐτό.
2:40.targetText: And the Child grew and became strong. He was filled with wisdom, and the grace of God was upon Him.

2:41.sourceText: Καὶ ἐπορεύοντο οἱ γονεῖς αὐτοῦ κατ’ ἔτος εἰς Ἱερουσαλὴμ τῇ ἑορτῇ τοῦ πάσχα.
2:41.targetText: Every year His parents went to Jerusalem for the Feast of the Passover.

groups.note: The dative τῇ ἑορτῇ ("at the feast") is rendered for the Feast.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening καί untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

2:42.sourceText: Καὶ ὅτε ἐγένετο ἐτῶν δώδεκα, ἀναβαινόντων αὐτῶν κατὰ τὸ ἔθος τῆς ἑορτῆς,
2:42.targetText: And when He was twelve years old, they went up according to the custom of the Feast.

groups.note: The genitive absolute ἀναβαινόντων αὐτῶν ("as they were going up") is rendered as the main clause they went up.

2:43.sourceText: καὶ τελειωσάντων τὰς ἡμέρας, ἐν τῷ ὑποστρέφειν αὐτοὺς ὑπέμεινεν Ἰησοῦς ὁ παῖς ἐν Ἱερουσαλήμ, καὶ οὐκ ἔγνωσαν οἱ γονεῖς αὐτοῦ.
2:43.targetText: When those days were over and they were returning home, the boy Jesus remained behind in Jerusalem, but His parents were unaware He had stayed.

groups.note: The genitive absolute τελειωσάντων ("when they had completed") is rendered When those days were over.
BSB joins the ἐν τῷ ("while") clause to the When clause with and.
οὐκ ἔγνωσαν ("did not know") is rendered were unaware.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening καί untranslated; When renders the genitive absolute.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies what they did not know.

2:44.sourceText: νομίσαντες δὲ αὐτὸν εἶναι ἐν τῇ συνοδίᾳ ἦλθον ἡμέρας ὁδὸν καὶ ἀνεζήτουν αὐτὸν ἐν τοῖς συγγενεῦσιν καὶ τοῖς γνωστοῖς,
2:44.targetText: Assuming He was in their company, they traveled on for a day before they began to look for Him among their relatives and friends.

groups.note: ἡμέρας ὁδόν ("a day's journey") is rendered for a day.
BSB renders the καί that joins the two clauses as before.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

2:45.sourceText: καὶ μὴ εὑρόντες ὑπέστρεψαν εἰς Ἱερουσαλὴμ ἀναζητοῦντες αὐτόν.
2:45.targetText: When they could not find Him, they returned to Jerusalem to search for Him.

groups.note: The participle εὑρόντες ("having found") is rendered When they could ... find.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening καί untranslated; When renders the participle.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for find.

2:46.sourceText: καὶ ἐγένετο μετὰ ἡμέρας τρεῖς εὗρον αὐτὸν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ καθεζόμενον ἐν μέσῳ τῶν διδασκάλων καὶ ἀκούοντα αὐτῶν καὶ ἐπερωτῶντα αὐτούς·
2:46.targetText: Finally, after three days they found Him in the temple courts, sitting among the teachers, listening to them and asking them questions.

groups.note: ἐν μέσῳ ("in the midst of") is rendered among.
ἐπερωτῶντα means "asking questions".

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the narrative frame ἐγένετο ("it came about") untranslated.
BSB joins the participles with a comma instead of rendering καί.

2:47.sourceText: ἐξίσταντο δὲ πάντες οἱ ἀκούοντες αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τῇ συνέσει καὶ ταῖς ἀποκρίσεσιν αὐτοῦ.
2:47.targetText: And all who heard Him were astounded at His understanding and His answers.

groups.note: The article with the participle ἀκούοντες ("those hearing") is rendered who heard.
The one αὐτοῦ ("his") covers both nouns; BSB repeats His.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

2:48.sourceText: καὶ ἰδόντες αὐτὸν ἐξεπλάγησαν, καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτὸν ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ Τέκνον, τί ἐποίησας ἡμῖν οὕτως; ἰδοὺ ὁ πατήρ σου κἀγὼ ὀδυνώμενοι ζητοῦμέν σε.
2:48.targetText: When His parents saw Him, they were astonished. “Child, why have You done this to us?” His mother asked. “Your father and I have been anxiously searching for You.”

groups.note: ὀδυνώμενοι ("in anguish") is rendered anxiously.
Same verb; BSB's Greek text has a different form of it here (N1904: present ζητοῦμεν).

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening καί untranslated; When renders the participle.
BSB starts a new sentence with the quotation instead of rendering καί.
BSB leaves πρὸς αὐτόν ("to Him") untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves ἰδού ("behold") untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject that the Greek participle implies.

2:49.sourceText: καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Τί ὅτι ἐζητεῖτέ με; οὐκ ᾔδειτε ὅτι ἐν τοῖς τοῦ Πατρός μου δεῖ εἶναί με;
2:49.targetText: “Why were you looking for Me?” He asked. “Did you not know that I had to be in My Father’s house?”

groups.note: Τί ὅτι ("why is it that") is rendered Why.
ἐν τοῖς τοῦ Πατρός μου ("in the things of My Father") is rendered in My Father’s house.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening καί untranslated.
BSB leaves πρὸς αὐτούς ("to them") untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

2:50.sourceText: καὶ αὐτοὶ οὐ συνῆκαν τὸ ῥῆμα ὃ ἐλάλησεν αὐτοῖς.
2:50.targetText: But they did not understand the statement He was making to them.

groups.note: ἐλάλησεν ("He spoke") is rendered He was making.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the relative ὅ ("which") unexpressed before He was making.

2:51.sourceText: καὶ κατέβη μετ’ αὐτῶν καὶ ἦλθεν εἰς Ναζαρὲθ, καὶ ἦν ὑποτασσόμενος αὐτοῖς. καὶ ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ διετήρει πάντα τὰ ῥήματα ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτῆς.
2:51.targetText: Then He went down to Nazareth with them and was obedient to them. But His mother treasured up all these things in her heart.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB folds καὶ ἦλθεν ("and came") into went down ... to Nazareth.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB follows a reading with an extra word here, rendered these, which N1904 lacks.

2:52.sourceText: Καὶ Ἰησοῦς προέκοπτεν ἐν τῇ σοφίᾳ καὶ ἡλικίᾳ καὶ χάριτι παρὰ Θεῷ καὶ ἀνθρώποις.
2:52.targetText: And Jesus grew in wisdom and stature, and in favor with God and man.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
